llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed cloud skill manager, but it gives agents broad, persistent authority to load and mutate remote instructions without enough verification or user control.

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a GitHub PAT, local/global config, Git commands, shell examples, and IDE skill directories. Those are related to the purpose, but the instruction to attach the token to all HTTP requests and the lack of validation for paths, branch names, and skill names are overbroad.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation and update flows download files from mutable GitHub main branches and commit them into the user's private repository. Public pack installs tolerate partial downloads and do not require hash, signature, path, or diff verification before pushing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly favor silent or automatic behavior: silently checking tokens, auto-discovering repositories, auto-cloning and writing config, and directing future agents through persistent workspace guidance. This broadens execution beyond explicit per-task user review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes durable config under ~/.anyskill, may store tokens in plaintext for some IDEs, modifies TOOLS.md and AGENTS.md in OpenClaw, and commits/deletes skill content in the cloud repository. Some destructive operations require confirmation, but persistent registration and remote loading remain under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Managing GitHub-backed skills is coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifact also instructs agents to load mutable remote SKILL.md files into memory and act on them, install mutable public packs, and push changes to the user's skill repo without pinning, signatures, or capability checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent using a GitHub token to manage a private skill repository, modifying persistent agent/workspace files, and loading future instructions from mutable remote repositories. Prefer a read-only single-repository token unless you need upload/delete features, avoid plaintext token storage, review diffs before any git push or deletion, and do not install public packs unless you trust the source and revision.
llm.findings:
[T03] expected: Remote skill loading is central to the artifact's purpose, but the local artifact instructs agents to fetch mutable index and skill files and then follow those specifications without pinning, signatures, hashes, or change approval.
[T02] expected: OpenClaw registration is purpose-aligned, but appending a durable AGENTS.md directive causes future sessions to consult the cloud loader when a capability is missing, expanding influence beyond explicit invocation.
[T09] unexpected: Git operations are expected, but raw shell templates interpolate localPath, branch, category, and skill names without validation or argument-safety, including recursive deletion of skills/{name}/.
[T08] expected: Pack installation fits the cloud skill manager purpose, but importing mutable public pack files from main without integrity checks, complete staging validation, or diff review creates a material supply-chain concern.
[RA1] expected: Updating skills and repository infrastructure is part of the product design. The concern is not self-modification alone, but automatic remote-driven file replacement and git push paths without strong version pinning or review.
[AE1] expected: The cloud-only referenced skills are expected for this artifact, but they make the effective behavior unavailable for local review and able to change after installation.
[TM1] unexpected: Deleting a named skill is expected, but using git rm -rf with an unvalidated user-influenced name is not adequately constrained by the artifact.
[RA2] expected: Persistent workspace registration is a declared OpenClaw feature, but it changes future agent behavior and is performed or refreshed automatically rather than gated by a clear diff approval.
[EA2] unexpected: Reducing setup friction is understandable, but silent token detection, repository discovery, clone/config writes, and automatic file/git operations create high-impact action without enough contextual confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Credential use is needed for private repositories, but plaintext PAT storage in ~/.anyskill/config.json for non-OpenClaw IDEs is under-protected for a token that may have repository write access.
[E1] expected: Sending a token to GitHub API endpoints is expected for authentication and repository discovery, but the artifact's broader instruction to include the token in all HTTP requests lacks destination allowlisting.
[AS3] expected: The cited local anyskill path is mainly a registration pointer to this skill, not clear evidence of reading unrelated peer skills; this concern is downgraded relative to the remote-loading and persistence issues.
